units.text: INT. ABANDONED SALT-LICK CHAPEL - DAY
A tin-roofed chapel on the edge of the alkali flats.
Pews pulled out and stacked against the wall.
In the middle of the floor, a block of rock salt the size of a coffin, glittering where the light finds it.
HOLLIS BRANDT-OKAFOR stands in the doorway, dust to his knees.
He is lean, sunburned, and carries a rifle like it weighs nothing.
He lets his eyes adjust.
Across the room, a woman sits on the altar rail with her boots swinging.
She does not look up when he enters.
She is peeling an orange with a skinning knife.
At the back, in the pulpit, a boy no older than fifteen crouches with a canvas sack in his arms.
He is trying to be invisible.
Mercy Calloway.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: Marshal Brandt. You're a long way from a courthouse.
units.name: MERCY

units.text: Forty miles. The horse died twenty back.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: She cuts a slice of orange and eats it.
Then you walked into the one place I know you'd come.
units.name: MERCY

units.text: The boy.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: He's not mine.
units.name: MERCY

units.text: That's not what the telegraph said.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: Telegraph says a lot.
units.name: MERCY

units.text: It said you took his father's payroll. It said you took the father, too.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: It said that.
units.name: MERCY

units.text: Did you?
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: Do you want me to say yes so you can hang me, or no so you can call me a liar?
units.name: MERCY

units.text: I want the truth.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: Then you're the first man in this territory who does.
units.name: MERCY

units.text: She finally looks at the boy.
He shrinks.
Tell him, Eli. Tell him what you saw.
units.name: MERCY

units.text: I -- my pa --
units.name: ELI

units.text: Easy, son.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: My pa shot first.
units.name: ELI

units.text: At who?
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: At her. She was only standing there.
units.name: ELI

units.text: Standing where?
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: By the well. She had the sack, she was giving it back.
units.name: ELI

units.text: I told you, boy, that's enough.
units.name: MERCY

units.text: No, let him finish.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: My pa wanted it for himself. He wanted all of it. He said if she lived, she'd talk.
units.name: ELI

units.text: And the father?
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: He fell in the well.
units.name: ELI

units.text: He fell. Not pushed. Fell.
units.name: MERCY

units.text: Eli, did she push him?
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: No, sir.
units.name: ELI

units.text: Then why did you run?
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: Because everybody said she did.
units.name: ELI

units.text: A long silence.
Salt ticks in the heat.
Outside, wind starts pulling at the tin roof.
I walked forty miles for a killer.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: And now?
units.name: MERCY

units.text: Now I've got a witness and a thief and a sack of money that belongs to a dead man's widow.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: That sounds like a mess, Marshal.
units.name: MERCY

units.text: It sounds like a trial.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: You'd put a fifteen-year-old on a stand against his own blood?
units.name: MERCY

units.text: I'd put the truth on a stand. He's just how it gets there.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: I'll do it.
units.name: ELI

units.text: Eli --
units.name: MERCY

units.text: I'll do it, Miss Mercy. Somebody ought to say it out loud.
units.name: ELI

units.text: Mercy slides off the altar rail.
She folds the knife and sets it on the salt block, handle toward Hollis.
Then I suppose I'm in your custody.
units.name: MERCY

units.text: I suppose you are.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: She holds out her wrists.
He doesn't take them.
He lifts the rifle, turns, and opens the chapel door to a white and blinding sky.
Walk with me. It's forty miles.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: And the boy?
units.name: MERCY

units.text: He walks too.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: The three of them step out into the glare.
